passages.text: Sequential Neural Networks as Automata William Merrill∗ Yale University, New Haven, CT, USA Allen Institute for Artiﬁcial Intelligence, Seattle, WA, USA william.merrill@yale.edu Abstract This work attempts to explain the types of computation that neural networks can perform arXiv:1906.01615v3 [cs.CL] 4 Jan 2021 by relating them to automata. We ﬁrst deﬁne what it means for a real-time network with bounded precision to accept a language. A measure of network memory follows from this deﬁnition.

passages.title: Sequential Neural Networks as Automata
passages.text: Weiss et al. (2018) propose a connection between long short- term memory networks (LSTMs) and counter au- tomata. They provide a construction by which the LSTM can simulate a simpliﬁed variant of a counter automaton. They also demonstrate that LSTMs can learn to increment and decrement their cell state as counters in practice.
